messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty PDR-2129 fired for az2 inference-host-network-errors (severity: high). Alert: consistent packet drops from 3 hosts in az2, causing gRPC streams to fail and KV cache evictions. Links: https://pd/realtime/PDR-2129 · runbook: infra/az-network-flap.md

pagerduty-bot: PDR-2129 assigned to oncall: Alice Wu. Escalation policy: SRE -> Eng-runtime.

Alice Wu: Acked PDR-2129. Jumping in — pulling logs and smoke tests. Anyone seeing customer-facing 5xxs?

Erika Singh: Support reporting 2 customer incidents in EU with increased latency and transient 500s on embedding endpoints since ~10:03 UTC. Customers: AcmeCorp, NoteApp.

Ben Kline: I'm IC for this incident. I'll coordinate with SRE. Alice, handoff to me once you have initial blast radius. I'll start incident doc.

Alice Wu: Quick findings: network telemetry shows interface RX errors on nodes redwood-az2-gpu-08/09/11. BGP sessions ok. Packet drop correlates with NIC driver logs: `mlx5_core` reporting "port flapping" and offload resets. KV cache eviction rate spike at 10:02 UTC.

Carla Mendes: Runtime seeing tail latency spike for small seq (<=64) -- timeouts from model shard manager when trying to fetch params from affected hosts. Canary routing has started fallback to az1 automatically.

Ben Kline: Customers currently degraded across az2 tenants; automated fallback is live but capacity in az1 is limited. Priority: stop evictions, ensure failover continues without overload, and notify customers.

David Cho: Spinning up extra ded instances in az3 and az1 with lower-priority models to absorb fallthrough. Command I ran: ```
# scale dedicated pool
infractl scale --pool inference-dedicated-az1 --replicas +12 --reason "az2 NIC flap fallback"
```

Alice Wu: Running drain on affected hosts to evacuate pods before NIC resets: ```
kubectl cordon node/redwood-az2-gpu-08
kubectl drain node/redwood-az2-gpu-08 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```  Will capture logs and then file hardware ticket with colo.

incident-bot: Note: automated fallback policy triggered for route: /v1/generate -> model: redwood-l2-large -> fallback: redwood-l2-medium. Fallback rate: 62% of requests in az2 zone.

Carla Mendes: Observability: tracing shows increased retry loop for seq requests; caches are warming slower. Suggest temporary increase of concurrency limit for fallback pools to reduce queue latency. Also recommend switching heavy-model traffic to batch endpoints.

Ben Kline: Agreed. Carla, coordinate with David to adjust concurrency. Alice, can you confirm eviction count and whether host NIC resets clear the condition or it recurs?

Alice Wu: Evictions so far: node-08 (1.2k), node-09 (900), node-11 (1.6k) in last 5m. NIC resets clear errors but then flip again after ~2-3 mins. Filing hardware escalation: HT-4321 to datacenter network ops.

Erika Singh: Drafting customer comms now: initial note to affected customers acknowledging degraded performance, describing fallback activation, and ETA for fix TBD. Will post to status.redwood.com if we confirm cross-AZ impact.

Ben Kline: Temporary mitigations checklist: 1) keep fallback routing active 2) scale az1/az3 pools (David) 3) cordon/drain flapping hosts (Alice) 4) throttle non-critical internal traffic (Carla) 5) open hardware ticket (Alice) 6) notify customers (Erika). Who's owning throttling?

Carla Mendes: I'll apply rate-limit for internal batch jobs: `routerctl set-rate --tag batch-infer --max-rps 120` and reduce cache prefetchers.

David Cho: Scale up confirmed: extra capacity online in az1/az3. Observed fallback success rate improving from 38% success to 85% on small requests after scaling and concurrency bump.

incident-bot: PDR-2129 status update: acknowledged -> investigating. Next check-in in 10 minutes.

Alice Wu: After drainage, node-08 NIC stabilized for 7m then flipped again. Datacenter reports link-level CRC errors on optical transceiver on rack 22. Replacing optics now.

Ben Kline: If optics replacement doesn't hold, we'll keep affected nodes cordoned and rely on fallback permanently for this incident. Plan for full failover if az2 loses >50% effective capacity.

Erika Singh: Customer comms posted to status page: "Partial degradation in az2 impacting inference latency and occasional errors. Automatic failover engaged; teams are mitigating. We will update in 30 minutes." Link: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/PDR-2129

Carla Mendes: Observing reduced KV cache evictions post-throttle and scaling. Latency 95p for gen reduced from 2.4s -> 950ms for affected tenants. Good signal.

David Cho: Can we enable scheduled fallback retention to avoid flip-flopping clients? Some clients are sticky to az2 and getting disrupted. Suggest setting `routing.fallback_min_duration=5m` to keep requests routed off unstable AZ for short term.

Ben Kline: Agreed. Carla, set fallback_min_duration=300s. Also start postmortem doc now and capture timeline. I'll tag eng-runtime, sres, and support.

Carla Mendes: Done: `routing set --fallback-min=300s --scope az2` 

incident-bot: PDR-2129 update: hardware team replaced transceiver on rack 22. Monitoring for stabilization.

Alice Wu: After replacement, node-09 errors cleared and node-08 has been stable for 12m. Eviction rates trending down. Continuing to monitor 30m before uncordon.

Erika Singh: Notifying AcmeCorp and NoteApp with updated status: "Partial impact reduced; engineering continuing mitigation. No ETA yet for full recovery."

Ben Kline: Good work everyone. Next actions: keep fallback, watch metrics for 30m, prepare rollback flags if anything regresses. I'll close the PD if stability holds for 30m. Assigning incident commander close-to-ready.

Alice Wu: Will uncordon nodes after 30m stable window, then observe load. Filing follow-up action items: hw follow-up with colo, update runbook with probe commands used, and add autopager refinement for NIC CRC pattern detection.

incident-bot: PDR-2129 updated: investigating -> monitoring. This thread will remain open until resolution.
